fixes.explanation: Micah says, “And He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land and tramples our citadels.” (Micah 5:5). Assyria is the nation invading in that verse. The ruler doesn't just bring peace. He IS the peace.

You got it, baker. The prophecy asks why she's crying aloud, then says anguish grips her like a woman in labor (Micah 4:9). It's a picture of real pain that's hard to ignore. I once got stuck in a stamper rack and thought THAT was pain. It was not even close.

Yes, baker. The text says, “there you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies!” (Micah 4:10). Babylon is the last place you'd expect a rescue to happen. Hearing "Babylon" and "rescued" in one breath is like a boss saying "you're fired" and "congratulations" in one sentence. The LORD does the redeeming, and He does it right there.

Right, baker. Micah 4:12 says they do not know the thoughts of the LORD or understand His plan. They gathered with their own plan in mind, saying “Let her be defiled…” (Micah 4:11). It's like showing up to a party sure you know what's going on, while everyone else is in on something you've never heard about. The LORD's plan was a different one.

Good guess, baker, but Kiriath Jearim isn't the town Micah names. Micah 5:2 says, “But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah…” Picture a ruler stepping out of a town so small you'd drive right past it. That's the one, Bethlehem Ephrathah.

Saul was a king of Israel (1 Samuel 10:1), so that's a good long way back, baker. But Micah 5:2 goes much further. It says the ruler's origins are “…of old, from the days of eternity.” Saul's days don't come close.

The judges were leaders the LORD raised up for Israel (Judges 2:16). That's old, baker, but Micah goes back further still. Micah 5:2 says this ruler's origins are “…from the days of eternity.” No judge's days can reach that far.

Close, baker, but nobody's giving a speech in this verse. Micah 5:3 says the rest of His brothers will return to the children of Israel. Think of folks finally walking back through the front door after a long time away. The word that fits is return.

I can see the thinking, baker, since the flock has been through a lot. But Micah 5:4 says the opposite of scattering: “And they will dwell securely…” With this shepherd standing in the strength of the LORD, they're secure.
That's how it sounds when a siege is in the news, baker. But Micah 5:4 says, “And they will dwell securely…” Hiding isn't in the picture. Securely is the word the text gives.
